candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite quantities so their fractional parts are comparable for subtraction by finding a common denominator, creating equivalent fractions, and when needed rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over the relevant denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or nonstandard mixed number into a usable subtraction form, such as expressing a whole number with a zero fractional part or converting an improper mixed number to a standard mixed number.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Borrow from the whole part when fractional subtraction would be negative and/or reduce the resulting fraction or zero form to lowest terms and final mixed-number or integer form.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms and present it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, or integer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: C uniquely separates simplification/final expression from regrouping and from the subtraction step itself. In A and B, these actions are bundled with regrouping in S04 or partially included in subtraction, so there is no standalone equivalent skill.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks agree strongly on denominator alignment and on the core subtraction step. The main structural difference is in how post-setup transformations are partitioned: A and B separate normalization from subtraction and combine regrouping with simplification, while C combines normalization with regrouping and separates simplification into its own skill. All expert skill_ids were mapped exactly once, preserving these granularity differences without making consolidation decisions.
